images.seen: A farmer hauling a blue tarp over hay bales on a bakkie while hail comes down, storm-dark sky and a lit farmhouse behind him. Friday.
lines: Hail on the way down and a tarp halfway on: this one is going to be close.
The sky is throwing ice and he is answering with a tarp.
Hail gives you about ninety seconds of warning, and he is using all of them.

images.seen: A big dog with wide eyes lying flat under the dining table, lightning forking outside the patio doors behind the chairs. Friday.
lines: The spot under the table was chosen scientifically: furthest from the sky.
Thunder counts double when you have ears like that.
One flash outside and the seating plan changed itself.

images.seen: An abandoned club cricket pitch under a black-green storm sky — covers half-dragged on, kit and jerseys dumped on the grass, the sightscreen blown askew. Thursday.
lines: Bad light stopped play, then the light got a lot worse.
The covers made it on; the kit did not make it off.
A sky that colour clears a cricket field faster than any umpire.

images.seen: A white plastic chair overturned in a roadside puddle, a yellow farmhouse behind, columns of rain falling from the dark cloud on the horizon. Wednesday.
lines: The first casualty is a plastic chair, and the storm is not even here yet.
That rain on the horizon is about ten minutes from this puddle.
The wind came through first and signed its work with one white chair.
